description: Configuration for the ERPNext MCP server: the master switch, the token an AI client authenticates with, the network allowlist, and one switch per tool.

fields.description: Master switch. While this is off the MCP endpoint answers 404 for everyone, whatever else is configured here. This is the fastest way to cut off an AI client: untick, save, done — no restart, no token change.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Token an MCP client must present, as X-MCP-Token (or Authorization: Bearer where the site's OAuth layer leaves it alone). Generated by the button below; stored encrypted and never shown again, logged or returned by any tool. Treat it as read access to your entire general ledger.
fields.label: Auth Token

fields.description: When the current token was created. Rotate it if it may have leaked.
fields.label: Token Generated On
Endpoint
fields.options:
Endpoint
POST https://<your-site>/api/method/erpnext_mcp.mcp.handle

Header
X-MCP-Token: <token>

JSON-RPC 2.0 (MCP Streamable HTTP). POST only — this server sends no unsolicited messages, so there is no stream to open.

Every call, allowed or refused, is recorded in MCP Action Log.

fields.description: The config an MCP client needs, generated from this site's own URL and token. The preview is masked; Copy and Download fetch the real token separately, so this panel is safe to leave open on a shared screen.
fields.label: Connect to Claude Desktop

fields.description: Comma- or newline-separated CIDR blocks allowed to reach the endpoint, checked after the token. Defaults to loopback plus private LAN ranges. An empty list denies everyone — a blank field is far more often a mistake than an intent to publish an accounting API. Add 0.0.0.0/0 only if you genuinely mean the whole internet.
fields.label: Allowed CIDRs

fields.description: Base URL a client should use, if it differs from the one this site sees. Leave empty and the connection panel uses frappe.utils.get_url(). Set it for a site behind a Tailscale Funnel, a tunnel or a reverse proxy on another hostname — there is no way for the server to guess its own public name. Example: https://erp.tail1234.ts.net
fields.label: Public URL

fields.description: On: tools run as the MCP System User below, so every document an AI created carries an owner that is obviously not a person, and every permission-checked tool (reports, attachments, comments, workflow actions) is bounded by that user's roles. Off: they run as Administrator, which works but makes MCP-authored documents indistinguishable from an admin's own. Leave this on unless you have a specific reason.
fields.label: Attribute Actions To An MCP System User

fields.description: The user tools run as, and that mutations are attributed to. Create a dedicated one (for example mcp@yourcompany.example) with only the roles the tools you enabled actually need — Accounts User is normally enough for the ledger tools; reports, attachments and workflow actions need whatever their own DocTypes require. Falls back to Administrator if left empty.
fields.label: MCP System User

fields.description: All on by default; none of these can change data. Turning one off removes it from the catalogue entirely, so a client cannot see it. Use this to keep an AI's view down to the job it is doing.
fields.label: Accounting Read Tools

fields.description: Map companies, cost centers, fiscal years and chart-of-accounts roots. The orientation call every client should make first.
fields.label: Get Company Topology

fields.description: Balance of one account as of a date, summed from GL Entry.
fields.label: Get Account Balance

fields.description: Paginated Journal Entry headers by date range, company, account and docstatus.
fields.label: Get Journal Entries

fields.description: One Journal Entry with every account line, party and reference.
fields.label: Get Journal Entry

fields.description: Bank Transactions by account, date range and status.
fields.label: List Bank Transactions

fields.description: One Bank Statement, where this ERPNext version has the doctype.
fields.label: Get Bank Statement

fields.description: Fiscal years and the companies they apply to.
fields.label: List Fiscal Years

fields.description: The chart of accounts as a nested tree.
fields.label: Get Chart Of Accounts

fields.description: Bank Transactions with money still unallocated.
fields.label: List Unreconciled Bank Transactions

fields.description: Fuzzy account lookup by number or name. Turn this off and a client must know exact docnames.
fields.label: Search Accounts

fields.description: Propose a complete numbered chart of accounts for a company from a static template, in the shape import_chart_of_accounts takes. Read-only: it reads the company's existing roots and account numbers so the proposal can flag collisions, and creates nothing.
fields.label: Propose Clean Chart

fields.description: Read-only. The company's cost centers as a nested tree, with numbers, group flags and disabled flags. Cost centers are the axis a posting is filed under alongside the account.
fields.label: List Cost Centers

fields.description:
Every one of these is off on a fresh install and stays off until you tick it. Each call is recorded in MCP Action Log with its arguments and its docstatus change. Enable the narrowest set that does the job: create_journal_entry alone gives an AI a scratchpad in the ledger, because a draft affects no balance until submit_journal_entry — a separate switch — posts it.

Two more write tools live in the sections below: Advance Workflow (Workflow) and Create Todo (Comments & Tasks). The banner at the top of this form always lists every write tool that is currently live, wherever its switch is.
fields.label: Accounting Write Tools

fields.description: Create a DRAFT Journal Entry (docstatus 0). Cannot submit. Balances are unaffected until something else submits it.
fields.label: Create Journal Entry

fields.description: Submit an existing draft Journal Entry (0 to 1). THIS MOVES BALANCES and writes GL Entries.
fields.label: Submit Journal Entry

fields.description: Cancel a submitted Journal Entry (1 to 2), writing reversing GL Entries. Requires a reason.
fields.label: Cancel Journal Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Set or change party_type and party on ONE line of a Journal Entry, including a submitted one, in both the voucher and its GL Entry rows. Moves no balance — account, debit, credit and date are not arguments. Requires a reason, which is written to the entry's comment thread.
fields.label: Update Journal Entry Party

fields.description: Insert a DRAFT Bank Transaction.
fields.label: Create Bank Transaction

fields.description: Attach payment vouchers to a Bank Transaction, up to its unallocated amount.
fields.label: Reconcile Bank Transaction

fields.description: WRITE. Create the Bank Account record a bank feed writes into, and the Bank institution behind it. Refuses a GL account that is not an Asset (a bank account) or a Liability (a credit card), and an Asset account whose account_type is not Bank or Cash — ERPNext's own reconciliation filters on that flag.
fields.label: Create Bank Account

fields.description: WRITE. Book a historical event as a DRAFT opening-balance journal entry, computing the offsetting line against Opening Balance Equity and flagging the entry as opening. Never submits.
fields.label: Set Opening Balance

fields.description: WRITE. Book a whole opening balance sheet as one journal entry — every line explicit, the balancing difference going to an offset account you name. Posts the entry too when asked, which also requires Submit Journal Entry above.
fields.label: Post Opening Balance Journal Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Submit many draft journal entries in one call, each in its own transaction so one failure does not undo the rest. Also requires Submit Journal Entry: that switch is where posting is allowed or not, and this one does not go round it.
fields.label: Bulk Submit Journal Entries

fields.description: WRITE. Delete a DRAFT journal entry outright, recording what it was and why in the audit log. Refuses submitted entries (cancel those instead) and cancelled ones — a cancelled entry and its reversing rows are the audit trail.
fields.label: Delete Draft Journal Entry

fields.description:
Structural changes to the chart itself, as opposed to postings into it. A bad journal entry is one wrong number a reversing entry fixes; a bad reparent silently changes what every balance-sheet subtotal has meant, retroactively, for every period already reported. Enable the narrowest set that does the job.

The read-only planner that produces a chart to review, Propose Clean Chart, is in the Accounting Read Tools section above. Import Chart Of Accounts defaults to a dry run even when it is switched on.
fields.label: Chart of Accounts

fields.description: WRITE. Create one account under an existing group. Validates the parent, the root type, the number's uniqueness and whether the account type can sit under that root before writing anything.
fields.label: Create Account

fields.description: WRITE. Rename, renumber, re-type or re-enable one account. Goes through ERPNext's own update_account_number so the docname moves with the fields. Cannot reparent.
fields.label: Update Account

fields.description: WRITE. Reparent one account. Moves no GL entry, but changes which subtotal every existing posting rolls up into, for every period already reported. The most consequential switch in this section.
fields.label: Move Account

fields.description: WRITE. Soft-delete an account. Requires a reason and refuses any account with GL entries in the current fiscal year. Nothing is deleted and it can be re-enabled.
fields.label: Disable Account

fields.description: WRITE. Build a whole tree of accounts from JSON in one transaction, rolling back entirely on any failure. Defaults to a dry run that creates nothing; a caller has to ask for the real one.
fields.label: Import Chart Of Accounts

fields.description: WRITE, AND IRREVERSIBLE — the only tool here with no undo, no draft and no cancelled state. Hard-deletes an account with no GL entries, no journal entry lines, no children, no company default and no bank account pointing at it. Prefer Disable Account for anything with history; this exists to free an account NUMBER, which disabling does not.
fields.label: Delete Account

fields.description: The calendar the ledger is allowed to post into. ERPNext refuses any posting whose date falls outside a fiscal year, and it refuses it from inside the document being saved — so booking anything historical needs the year to exist first. Creating one books nothing and moves no balance.
fields.label: Fiscal Years

fields.description: WRITE. Create a Fiscal Year so ERPNext will accept postings dated inside it — the prerequisite for booking anything historical. Refuses a name already in use and a date range overlapping another year for the same company.
fields.label: Create Fiscal Year

fields.description: WRITE. Move a fiscal year's dates or enable/disable it. Refuses a move that would leave existing GL entries outside any fiscal year, and cannot rename the year or change which companies it applies to.
fields.label: Update Fiscal Year

fields.description:
How a posting is classified once it reaches an account: which segment of the business it belongs to (cost centers), what other axes it is filed under (accounting dimensions), and which accounts a document reaches for when nothing says (company defaults).

The read-only tree, List Cost Centers, is in the Accounting Read Tools section above. Create Accounting Dimension is the only switch in this app that can add a DocType to your site — and only when a call asks for it explicitly.
fields.label: Cost Centers & Dimensions

fields.description: WRITE. Create one cost center under an existing group. Validates the parent and the number's uniqueness before writing anything. Cannot create a root: ERPNext gives every company exactly one, named after the company.
fields.label: Create Cost Center

fields.description: WRITE. Rename, renumber or disable/enable one cost center. Moves the docname with the fields. Cannot reparent — this app ships no tool that can.
fields.label: Update Cost Center

fields.description: WRITE, AND A SCHEMA CHANGE. Creates an Accounting Dimension and adds a Link custom field to the documents that carry it — and, when the call asks for it, generates the custom DocType whose records become the dimension's values. Those fields are permanent until somebody removes them in the Desk. The narrowest switch in this section to leave off.
fields.label: Create Accounting Dimension

fields.description: WRITE. Add one value to an existing accounting dimension — one record in the DocType that dimension points at. Touches no ledger and creates no fields.
fields.label: Create Dimension Value

fields.description: WRITE. Point the company's default account and cost center fields at real accounts, type-checked (a Receivable field has to name a Receivable account). Changes no existing posting, only what the next document picks by default. Idempotent.
fields.label: Set Company Defaults

fields.description: Reading a site's approval structure, and — behind its own switch — acting on it. Workflow actions run through Frappe's own apply_workflow, so they respect the acting user's roles and the transition's conditions.
fields.label: Workflow

fields.description: Every Workflow definition: governed DocType, states, transitions and roles.
fields.label: List Workflows

fields.description: Where one document sits in its workflow and which transitions lead out of that state.
fields.label: Get Workflow State

fields.description: Documents parked in a state that still has an action available, optionally narrowed to one user's roles.
fields.label: List Pending Approvals

fields.description: Which workflow actions the acting MCP user can take on a document right now.
fields.label: List Available Actions

fields.description: WRITE. Take a workflow action on a document via Frappe's apply_workflow. Moves state and can submit or cancel the document, exactly as the Desk button does.
fields.label: Advance Workflow

fields.description: A site's saved reports are usually the most trustworthy answer to an accounting question, because somebody who knew the schema already wrote them. run_report enforces the acting user's permission on the report's DocType, so it can reach figures the raw read tools cannot — and is bounded by the roles you gave the MCP System User.
fields.label: Reports

fields.description: Every saved Report, its ref_doctype and its report_type.
fields.label: List Reports

fields.description: Run a Query, Script or Report Builder report and return its rows. Respects the acting user's permission on the report's DocType. Reports often expose figures the individual read tools do not.
fields.label: Run Report

fields.description: The read tools check read permission on the parent document before returning anything, and treat an unattached private file as its owner's. Turn Get Attachment Content off if files on this site hold anything an AI client should never read. Attach File To Document writes, needs write permission on the parent, and is off by default.
fields.label: Attachments

fields.description: Files attached to a document. Checks read permission on that document.
fields.label: List Attachments

fields.description: Base64 content of one attachment, size-capped. Honours private-file permissions. Turn this off if attachments on this site hold anything an AI client should not read.
fields.label: Get Attachment Content

fields.description: WRITE. Attach a file to ANY document — a statement onto the Journal Entry that books it, a receipt onto a Bank Transaction, a contract onto an Asset. Creates one File and changes nothing else. Needs write permission on the parent document, refuses a cancelled parent unless told otherwise, and refuses a filename the document already has.
fields.label: Attach File To Document

fields.description: The human layer: what people said about a document, and what is on somebody's list. List Comments checks read permission on the document. Create Todo writes.
fields.label: Comments & Tasks

fields.description: The comment and activity thread on a document. Checks read permission on that document.
fields.label: List Comments

fields.description: ToDo rows assigned to a user.
fields.label: List Assigned Todos

fields.description: WRITE. Assign a ToDo to a user. Touches no ledger, but it does put an item in somebody's queue and notify them.
fields.label: Create Todo

fields.description: Only usable where the Frappe HR (hrms) app is installed — on a site without it these tools are not advertised at all, whatever these switches say. Employee, attendance and leave data is personal information; enable deliberately.
fields.label: HR

fields.description: Employee records with department, designation and status.
fields.label: List Employees

fields.description: Per-employee counts of Present / Absent / Half Day / On Leave over a date range.
fields.label: Get Attendance Summary

fields.description: Remaining leave per type for one employee, computed by HR's own balance function.
fields.label: Get Leave Balance

fields.description: Order books and receivables ageing, from ERPNext's Selling, Buying and Accounts modules.
fields.label: Sales & Purchasing

fields.description: Sales Order headers with totals and delivery progress.
fields.label: List Sales Orders

fields.description: Submitted Sales Invoices still owed, with ageing buckets.
fields.label: Get Outstanding Invoices

fields.description: Purchase Order headers with totals and receipt progress.
fields.label: List Purchase Orders

fields.description: Site customisation, for a developer debugging their own instance. Client Script bodies are truncated to 500 characters.
fields.label: Meta

fields.description: Custom Fields on this site, in form order. For debugging why a field is not appearing.
fields.label: List Custom Fields

fields.description: Client Scripts with a truncated preview of each body.
fields.label: List Client Scripts

fields.description:
Structured artefacts for somebody who has to sign something off — each carries its own provenance and its own anomaly flags, and an ERROR flag means the numbers do not internally agree. All read-only: nothing is stored, emailed or filed.

The first two switches are the MCP tools; the rest are the individual packet types, each gated separately so you can expose a reconciliation packet without exposing a payroll one.
fields.label: Compliance Packets

fields.description: Which packet types this site can produce, and the filters each takes. Discovery only.
fields.label: List Compliance Packets

fields.description: Build a packet and return it inline. Nothing is stored, emailed or filed. Reads only what the packet needs.
fields.label: Generate Compliance Packet

fields.description: One account, one period: opening and closing balances, every Journal Entry that touched it, the drafts that would change it, the cancellations a balance query cannot see, and a check that the arithmetic closes.
fields.label: Reconciliation Packet

fields.description: A year for an outside CPA: trial balance, income statement, balance sheet, twenty largest entries, intercompany activity, document counts, and a check that the accounting identity holds.
fields.label: Fiscal Year Audit Packet

fields.description: The member register and its event trail. The cap table is the only place on this site that maps an anonymous member id to a legal name — gate it accordingly.
fields.label: Cap Table and Member Events

fields.description: READ. One company's member register: anonymous id, legal entity name, entity type, admission and withdrawal dates, ownership percentage. This is the tool that de-anonymises the ledger, so turning it off is a real choice.
fields.label: List Cap Table

fields.description: WRITE. Register one member: the anonymous id the ledger is tagged with, and the legal entity behind it. Refuses a duplicate member id, and an id that is not already a value of the Member accounting dimension.
fields.label: Create Cap Table Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Change a member's legal name, entity type, admission date, percentage, cost center or notes. Cannot retire a member and cannot change the member id.
fields.label: Update Cap Table Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Retire a member: withdrawal date, retired flag, and a Withdrawal event in the trail. Moves no money — a final distribution is a separate Record Member Event call.
fields.label: Close Cap Table Entry

fields.description: READ. Contributions, distributions, admissions, withdrawals, transfers and reallocations, with the narrative for each and the journal entry that books it.
fields.label: List Member Events

fields.description: WRITE. Record one member event and, where it books money, the DRAFT journal entry for it — tagged with the member dimension on every line. Enabling this grants creating that draft; it does not grant posting it.
fields.label: Record Member Event

fields.description: WRITE. Post the draft journal entry a member event is waiting on. Also requires Submit Journal Entry to be on — that switch is where moving a balance is decided, whatever route reaches it.
fields.label: Submit Member Event

fields.description: The durable archive: operating agreements, trust documents, resolutions, prior statements, and the amendment chain between them.
fields.label: Governance Documents

fields.description: READ. What is in the archive, with the amendment chain and which entries are still operative.
fields.label: List Governance Documents

fields.description: READ. One archived document's metadata and the bytes of its attachment, base64. Enforces read permission on the document, like the other attachment tools.
fields.label: Read Governance Document

fields.description: WRITE. File a governing document, attach its content as a private file, and chain it onto whatever it supersedes. Refuses a duplicate title and a circular chain.
fields.label: Attach Governance Document

fields.description: Assets that serve more than one part of the business, and assets that are financed. Depreciation written here is split by usage and is always a draft.
fields.label: Assets and Depreciation

fields.description: READ. For every financed asset, whether its remaining depreciation and its note's remaining term still agree, and by how many months they do not.
fields.label: Depreciation / Note Alignment Check

fields.description: WRITE. Create an ERPNext Asset plus the cost profile holding its usage split and schedule. Switches ERPNext's own depreciation OFF on that asset, because this app then owns the schedule and both running would depreciate it twice.
fields.label: Create Asset

fields.description: WRITE. Replace an asset's cost center split. Not retroactive: periods already written keep the split they were written with.
fields.label: Update Asset Allocation

fields.description: WRITE. Tie an asset to the note that financed it, refusing by default unless its useful life equals the note's tenor so paid-off and fully-depreciated fall in the same month.
fields.label: Link Asset to Note

fields.description: WRITE. Write the depreciation due up to a date as draft journal entries, split across each asset's cost centers. Dry run by default; every period written is recorded so it cannot be written twice.
fields.label: Run Depreciation Cycle

fields.description: What the company owes and on what terms. A payment produces a draft journal entry; closing a note posts nothing at all.
fields.label: Notes Payable

fields.description: READ. Every note or loan a company owes: lender, original and outstanding principal, rate, term, and when the next payment falls due.
fields.label: List Notes Payable

fields.description: WRITE. Register an outstanding note: its terms, its provenance, the liability account it posts to, and the asset it financed. Refuses by default when a linked asset's useful life and the note's term disagree.
fields.label: Create Note Payable

fields.description: WRITE. Split a payment into principal and interest and draft the journal entry that books it, decrementing the note's outstanding balance. Never submits.
fields.label: Record Loan Payment

fields.description: WRITE. Close a note as Paid Off, Refinanced or Written Off, recording the disposition in its own history. Writes no journal entry — relieving a written-off balance is a posting with tax consequences that somebody should make on purpose.
fields.label: Close Note Payable

fields.description: The land register and the leases over it. Nothing in this group posts: a lease with rent on it produces no journal entry, and linking a parcel to a Fixed Asset moves no balance.
fields.label: Real Estate

fields.description: READ. One entity's land register with acreage and appraised value totalled, and the oldest and newest appraisal dates.
fields.label: List Parcels

fields.description: READ. One parcel in full, with the leases over it and the Fixed Asset carrying it.
fields.label: Get Parcel

fields.description: WRITE. Register a parcel: county, assessor parcel id, acreage, use type, appraised value and the date it was appraised as of. Refuses a duplicate name or a duplicate assessor id inside one entity.
fields.label: Create Parcel

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered parcel. Cannot re-key it, cannot move it between entities, and cannot set the asset link — that is its own tool.
fields.label: Update Parcel

fields.description: WRITE. Point a parcel at the Fixed Asset carrying it and report the gap between cost and appraised value. Sets one field; posts nothing.
fields.label: Link Parcel to Asset

fields.description: WRITE. Move a Parcel to another Company as a conveyance: the parcel record, its attachments, and every lease, block, irrigation zone, housing unit and housing assignment pointing at it. Writes no Journal Entry — recording a conveyance and booking its consequences are separate acts. Refuses over an active lease.
fields.label: Convey Parcel

fields.description: READ. Leases in both directions with the annual rent roll, and which ones run out soon. Never expires a lease itself.
fields.label: List Leases

fields.description: READ. One lease in full, with the parcel it covers and its attachments.
fields.label: Get Lease

fields.description: WRITE. Record a lease in either direction, with the executed document attached. Books nothing — recording the agreement and booking its consequences are separate acts.
fields.label: Create Lease

fields.description: WRITE. Change a recorded lease's status, term, rent or parties. Refuses to mark one Terminated without a termination date.
fields.label: Update Lease

fields.description: The governance register of who is related to the company and how. Separate from the Party field on a Journal Entry, which is unaffected by anything here.
fields.label: Related Parties

fields.description: READ. The related-party register, current and ended, and which relationships have no governing document behind them.
fields.label: List Related Parties

fields.description: READ. One relationship with everything pointing at it. Never returns more than four digits of a taxpayer id, including from a linked Supplier.
fields.label: Get Related Party

fields.description: WRITE. Register a relationship. Stores the last four digits of a taxpayer id and refuses nine — the full number belongs on the signed W-9, not on this site.
fields.label: Create Related Party

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered relationship. Cannot re-key it: a change of role is a new relationship, and the old entry gets an end date rather than being deleted.
fields.label: Update Related Party

fields.description: Tools that build a document — a PDF report, a tax workbook — and file it in the governance archive with the file attached. They create a Governance Document and Files; they post nothing to the ledger.
fields.label: Generated Documents

fields.description: WRITE. Build the quarter's investment report as a PDF and file it as a Prior Statement. Refuses a quarter that is not genuinely closed — the statement filed, every investment entry submitted, every bank transaction reconciled — and names everything missing in one reply.
fields.label: Generate Quarterly Investment Report

fields.description: WRITE. Aggregate a year of supplier payments into a 1099-NEC workbook and per-recipient forms. A PRE-FILL: taxpayer ids print as the last four digits only, and Copy A is stamped as an information copy rather than a filing.
fields.label: Generate 1099-NEC Pre-Fill

fields.description: READ. Every company with its abbreviation, currency, tax-id status, fiscal year period, cost center and account counts, and the GL entry count with first and last posting dates.
fields.label: List Companies

fields.description: WRITE. Stand up a Company plus its chart of accounts, cost centers and the fiscal year containing today. Refuses a duplicate name or abbreviation, an unknown country or currency, and a non-group parent.
fields.label: Create Company

fields.description: WRITE. Change a company's country, tax id or notes — and its currency only while nothing is posted. Refuses the abbreviation, the name, and the fiscal year start month, each with the reason.
fields.label: Update Company

fields.description: WRITE. Register the Family and Contact Party Types so a Journal Entry line can carry them. Idempotent, and already seeded on install and on every migrate. Changes no existing record.
fields.label: Register Party Types

fields.description: READ. The block register with acreage totalled, plantings summarised, and the varieties already in use on this site.
fields.label: List Fields

fields.description: READ. One block in full, with its irrigation zones, their water rights, and how much of the block is not zoned.
fields.label: Get Field

fields.description: READ. One parcel rolled up: blocks, planted acres against the parcel's own, zones, flow, planting ages, and the food-safety gaps.
fields.label: Parcel Field Summary

fields.description: READ. The zone register with area and flow totalled, plus the zones with no water test and the surface-water zones with no water right.
fields.label: List Irrigation Zones

fields.description: READ. One zone in full, with the block it waters and that block's share of it.
fields.label: Get Irrigation Zone

fields.description: WRITE. Register a planted block under a parcel, with its food-safety facts. Refuses a duplicate name on one parcel, a claimed Farm App id, and blocks summing to more acres than the parcel has.
fields.label: Create Field

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered block. Cannot re-key it, cannot move it to another parcel, and cannot set the cost center — that is its own tool.
fields.label: Update Field

fields.description: WRITE. Point a block at the Cost Center its costs book to. Sets one field; posts nothing and moves no existing entry.
fields.label: Link Field to Cost Center

fields.description: WRITE. Create Fields from a batch of legacy Farm App records carrying their ids. Dry run by default, whole batch validated before the first insert, never updates an existing record.
fields.label: Import Farm App Fields

fields.description: WRITE. Register a zone under a block. Refuses a duplicate zone name on the parcel, a zone number already used on that block, and zones summing to more area than the block.
fields.label: Create Irrigation Zone

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered zone. Cannot re-key it, cannot move it to another block, and cannot set the area in acres — that is computed.
fields.label: Update Irrigation Zone

fields.description: READ. The camp register with capacity, occupancy and open beds, plus the overdue inspections, the uninhabitable units and the ones filled past what their floor area allows.
fields.label: List Housing Units

fields.description: READ. One unit in full with its whole assignment history, and the compliance gaps named in sentences.
fields.label: Get Housing Unit

fields.description: READ. Who is housed where, currently or over a period, with the wage-deduction assignments named and the deposits still held.
fields.label: List Housing Assignments

fields.description: READ. Beds, bodies and overdue inspections per parcel and in total, with a plain readout.
fields.label: Housing Capacity

fields.description: READ. Everywhere one person has been housed, in order, with deposits and wage deductions.
fields.label: Employee Housing History

fields.description: WRITE. Register a building on a camp with its compliance facts. Computes the lawful occupancy from floor area unless one is given.
fields.label: Create Housing Unit

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered unit. Cannot re-key it and cannot move it between parcels.
fields.label: Update Housing Unit

fields.description: WRITE. Put one person in one unit from a date. Refuses an overlapping assignment unless multi-occupancy is asked for, a non-residential unit, an uninhabitable one, and an unknown employee where an HR app is installed.
fields.label: Create Housing Assignment

fields.description: WRITE. Write the date somebody moved out and the deposit returned. Never deletes: the record is the audit trail for IRS Section 119 and for a wage claim.
fields.label: End Housing Assignment

fields.description: READ. Which blocks a GPS fix is inside. Bounding box first, then exact point-in-polygon; the boundary counts as inside. This is the geofence query.
fields.label: Find Fields Containing a Point

fields.description: READ. Which blocks an H3 cell touches, at any resolution. The spatial-index join for anything else keyed on H3.
fields.label: Find Fields by H3 Cell

fields.description: WRITE. Give a block its GeoJSON polygon and derive centroid, bounding box, H3 coverage and area from it. Refuses invalid or self-intersecting shapes, coordinates off Earth, and an area more than 25% from the recorded acreage.
fields.label: Set Field Boundary

fields.description: WRITE. The same for an irrigation zone, and reports whether it sits inside the block it waters — reported rather than enforced, because a shared line really does cross boundaries.
fields.label: Set Zone Boundary
